header.account: A US criminal and traffic defense law firm
header.summary: The bidding setup mostly fits the volume, but the account is changing faster than the bidder can learn: 6 of 9 campaigns are settling after budget and target edits, so most verdicts wait until Oct 15. One campaign has a CPA target on about 3 conversions a month, one target looks too loose on Google's own simulation, the two biggest campaigns are held back by budget rather than bidding, and no conversion carries a value yet.

red_flags.flag: CPA up while impression share falls
red_flags.rule: CPA worsening (10%+ vs prior 30 days) and search impression share down 5+ points
red_flags.detail: Worsening CPA: DUI (CPA +39%, impression share -3 points), Drug Charges (CPA +14%, impression share flat), Out-of-State Traffic (CPA +129%, impression share flat). Impression share down 5+ points: Traffic Tickets (71% to 53%, CPA +6%), Nursing Board (94% to 79%, CPA -24%), Criminal Defense (35% to 27%, CPA -38%). No campaign has both.

red_flags.rule: last 4 complete weeks, weeks with 3+ conversions: highest weekly CPA more than 2x the lowest
red_flags.detail: Traffic Tickets: $19 to $36 (1.9x) over 4 readable weeks; Out-of-State DUI: 0 weeks with 3+ conversions, too few to read (data fit already covers it); Out-of-State Traffic: $29 to $38 (1.3x) over 3 readable weeks.

red_flags.applies_to: ROAS targets and Maximize conversion value
red_flags.rule: 30-day value per conversion 20%+ below the prior 30 days while conversions rose
red_flags.detail: not graded: no campaign bids on value, and 30-day conversion value is $0

red_flags.flag: Missing its target while limited by budget
red_flags.applies_to: campaigns with a CPA or ROAS target
red_flags.rule: calibration warn or fail and Google reports LIMITED_BY_BUDGET
red_flags.detail: Traffic Tickets is limited by budget, but its CPA is 1.03x the $23 target (on target).

next_steps: Agree a value for each lead type with the firm (for example, average fee times the share of calls, forms and chats that become cases). Ask before using any number.
Set those values on the counted actions (update_conversion_action, after confirmation), or better, send signed-case values back through the existing imported conversion action.
Fix the imported action's counting to one per click in Google Ads, so repeat calls do not inflate values.
Collect 30 days of values, then re-run this skill. Traffic Tickets and Criminal Defense are the first candidates for Maximize conversion value.

recommendations.change: Freeze bids and budgets until Oct 15, then make the changes below in one batch
recommendations.why: 6 of 9 campaigns are inside a settling window, and budgets were edited on 3 separate days in 30, including a bulk edit of every budget on Oct 1 that was redone 22 seconds later (counted here as one edit round). Each round restarts the bidder's learning.
recommendations.who: do this in Google Ads (no edits)

recommendations.change: On Oct 15, Out-of-State DUI: drop the $22 CPA target and keep Maximize conversions
recommendations.why: 2.9 conversions a month is far below the 15 a CPA target needs to calibrate. The target was added on Sep 28 when the campaign moved off Maximize clicks.
recommendations.who: do this in Google Ads: the update_campaign action refuses a switch to the strategy a campaign already runs, so it cannot drop a target on its own
recommendations.success_check: on Oct 29, CPA since Oct 15 within 30% of the 30-day CPA on Oct 15, and conversions not lower than the 2 weeks before
recommendations.rollback: if CPA from Oct 15 to Oct 29 is more than 1.3x the 30-day CPA on Oct 15, return to Maximize clicks with a CPC limit on Oct 29

recommendations.change: Out-of-State Traffic: on Oct 15, if CPA since Sep 28 is still above the target, step the target from $30 back to $25 (-17%)
recommendations.why: 30-day CPA $39 is above the $30 target. Google's simulation for Sep 25 to Oct 1 prices the conversions between 0.75x and 1x the target ($22.50 to $30) at about $227 each; at 0.75x, weekly cost falls 20% for 9% fewer conversions. That week includes the Sep 28 change from $25 to $30, so it mixes both targets: read the simulation again on Oct 15 before acting.
recommendations.who: I can do this after you confirm
recommendations.success_check: on Oct 29, CPA since Oct 15 at or under $25, with no more than 10% fewer conversions than the 2 weeks before
recommendations.rollback: if conversions from Oct 15 to Oct 29 are more than 25% below the 2 weeks before, go back to $30 on Oct 29
recommendations.run: not run: waits for your yes

recommendations.change: Traffic Tickets and Criminal Defense: leave the bidding alone; the budget is what limits them
recommendations.why: Traffic Tickets runs at 1.03x the $23 target and loses 27% of impression share to budget; Criminal Defense has the account's lowest non-brand CPA ($19) and loses 41% to budget.
recommendations.who: budget changes are out of scope here; use budget-allocation-optimizer if installed

what_not_to_do: Don't tighten Traffic Tickets' CPA target, or add one to Criminal Defense, to 'save money': Traffic Tickets is on its $23 target and Criminal Defense (no target) has the lowest non-brand CPA, and both are limited by budget, so a tighter target would only cut volume.
Don't judge the Sep 28 strategy and target changes before their re-check dates; a week of data on a few conversions is noise.
Don't switch anything to Target ROAS or Maximize conversion value until conversions carry real values.
